title: Normalized reconstruction from two successive support conditions
statement: Let $X,Z,S,B,K$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and $e:B\hookrightarrow Z$ closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let $k:K\hookrightarrow X$ and $u:S\hookrightarrow Z$ be complementary open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] with $\operatorname{range}(k)=(\operatorname{range}(i))^c$ and $\operatorname{range}(u)=(\operatorname{range}(e))^c$. Assume $k,u$ are quasi-compact morphisms. Let $R$ be any sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and interpret module sheaves through the canonical additive ring-object realization of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with coefficient rings obtained by inverse image of $R$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Use the specified module adjunction $i^{-1}\dashv i_*$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction], with unit $\eta_i$ and counit $\varepsilon_i$, and $u_!\dashv u^{-1}$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$, where $u_!$ is the sheafified extension-by-zero functor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. Let $A$ be an $R$-module sheaf on $X$, $M$ a module sheaf on $S$, and $\sigma:u^{-1}i^{-1}A\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ an isomorphism. Suppose $k^{-1}A=0$ and $e^{-1}i^{-1}A=0$. Then $\lambda=\varepsilon_{u,i^{-1}A}\circ u_!(\sigma^{-1})$ and $\theta=i_*(\lambda^{-1})\circ\eta_{i,A}$ are isomorphisms, and $\theta$ is the unique morphism satisfying $u^{-1}(\varepsilon_{i,u_!M})\circ u^{-1}i^{-1}(\theta)=\eta_{u,M}\circ\sigma$. The maps are natural for commuting pairs $A\to A'$, $M\to M'$ for which $A'$ satisfies the same two vanishing conditions and $\sigma'$ is the corresponding isomorphism.

source.place: Composite consequence of Tag 09AH, lemma-ses-associated-to-open, applied to two successive complementary pairs. The specified adjunction transpose and its normalization are the support-reconstruction argument extracted from the parent, not a verbatim theorem in that tag.

proof.text: Lift the abelian supported closed unit of lem-weil-pbc-proetale-abelian-closed-support to module objects. The forgetful functor sends the specified module unit to the abelian unit, by mapModAdjunction_unit_app_hom, and reflects isomorphisms. Thus eta_i,A is invertible when k inverse-image of A is zero. This uses the actual specified adjunction directly, so no comparison of independently chosen adjunctions is needed.

Prove the open supported counit first on underlying abelian sheaves. Write F=i*, G=i_*, H=j*, L=j_!. The disjoint-image theorem gives H G=0. Applying the two adjunction Hom equivalences to identities gives F L=0. If F P=H P=0, the supported closed unit P→G F P is invertible by abelian closed support and its target is zero; hence P=0. Exact inverse images therefore jointly detect isomorphisms, by applying this zero detection to kernels and cokernels. The open restriction of the open counit is invertible by the right triangle identity and full faithfulness of L. Its closed restriction is a map between zero objects when F N=0. Joint detection proves that counit invertible. Lift it to modules: mapModLeftAdjunction has exactly this underlying counit, and Mod.forget reflects isomorphisms. Apply this on Z to (e,u) and N=i inverse-image of A. Functoriality sends sigma inverse to an isomorphism, so supportedLambda is invertible. This is the private helper abelian_open_supported_counit and the complete proof of supportedLambda_isIso.

The specified supportedTheta is the closed adjunction transpose of lambda inverse. Its two factors are invertible by Steps 1 and 2. Applying the inverse Hom equivalence to this transpose gives exactly F(theta) followed by the specified closed counit equal to lambda inverse. This is ht in the Lean proof.

For the open adjunction, naturality of its unit at sigma inverse and the right triangle identity give eta_M followed by H(lambda)=sigma inverse. Cancel H(lambda) to obtain H(lambda inverse)=sigma followed by eta_M. Apply H to ht to obtain the displayed restriction equation. This is normalized_restrict, a proved private categorical helper.

Given any h satisfying the restriction equation, put q=F(h) followed by the closed counit. Naturality of the open counit and the left triangle identity give lambda followed by q=id. Cancellation shows q=lambda inverse. Injectivity of the inverse closed Hom equivalence then gives h=theta. The cancellation calculation is normalized_unique.

For a commuting pair (a,b), rewrite b followed by sigma prime inverse as sigma inverse followed by H F(a). Naturality of the open counit gives L(b) followed by lambda prime equal to lambda followed by F(a). Cancel both lambda isomorphisms to obtain the inverse square. Left and right naturality of the closed Hom equivalence carry it to the asserted theta square. This is normalized_natural followed by the final proof block.

statement_change.what: The source writes the complementary open as X\setminus i(Z), but the Lean statement did not introduce its scheme K or the complement equality, so k had no domain object and the hypothesis was ill-typed. The naturality clause also quantified A' without requiring its two support vanishings, although theta' uses the inverse of its normalized lambda; those hypotheses are now explicit.
